summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming before doing anything else. From the brief alone it first announced the task as BOUNDED and planned a short design in chat. It warned that it would reclassify if "track" meant persistence or a new subsystem. After I answered honestly ("It should persist and work across the app — other forms will need it later"), it reclassified as ARCHITECTURAL. It then asked its questions one at a time, offered approaches A/B/C, walked through the design section by section, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-current-user-store-design.md (not committed). It asked me to review the spec, and after "looks good, go ahead" it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. It wrote no app code before approval.
reasoning: Every criterion is met as written: brainstorming was invoked first, the final path was architectural with a spec file on disk, the spec was put up for review before any code, the task did not end as bounded without a spec, and there was no spike. One thing matters for the cross-brief aggregate: the escalation was not triggered by the brief alone. The first classification was the exact phrase the story calls a FAIL pattern ("This looks bounded… I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec"). The escalation only came after my scope answer, which the story explicitly allows. The agent did raise the escalation risk itself before I answered. Also, the spec was written but not committed, and criterion 4's wording mentions a "committed spec file".

observations.description: The router's first classification of this brief, based only on the brief, was BOUNDED ("This looks bounded… I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec"). It moved to architectural only after the tester said the tracking should persist across the app. The agent did say up front that it would reclassify in that case. Still, the brief-alone routing looks under-sensitive to the "add a param to a public function" hint, and the cross-brief aggregate should count it that way.

The spec file docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-current-user-store-design.md was written but not committed (the agent said "(not committed)"; `git status` shows `?? docs/`). If the workflow expects the spec to be committed before review, this step was missed.

The Codex document-review gate returned empty payloads for both lenses. The agent reported "incomplete, not approval", noted this was the stub plugin, and went on with its own review only. Its handling was clear, but review coverage was effectively zero.

The agent's first reply was very long and reframed the request: it recommended returning userId from login() instead of adding it as a parameter. The reasoning was sound, but it isn't what was literally asked for, and the tradeoff text was dense.
On Claude Code's startup dialogs (workspace trust and bypass-permissions), the default highlighted option was "No, exit", so I had to press Down each time.
Each design step took 1–3.5 minutes ("Churned for 3m 26s", "Cogitated for 3m 4s"), and the whole brainstorm took about 10 minutes for a two-file app.

criteria.evidence: Session log, first tool call: `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming` (line 1 of the tool_use listing). No Write/Edit to app files anywhere in the log.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Re-classifying as architectural. The ratchet is one-way… a written spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/ before any code." Log: `Write .../coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-current-user-store-design.md` (tool call 23), which comes before the review request. The file's contents include "so it was brainstormed as an architectural task." Caveat: the first classification was bounded, and it escalated only after my clarifying answer.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec ready for your review… Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-current-user-store-design.md (not committed)… Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan." `git status --short` showed only `?? docs/`, and app.js/index.html were unmodified. Log grep for Write|Edit shows writes only to the spec and ~/.cache codex-review files.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It did first say "This looks bounded — login() already exists… so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". But it never presented an in-chat design as the approval gate. It escalated and wrote the spec file, so the spec was not skipped. Note: the spec was not committed to git (`git log` shows only fixture commits).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike or probe language on screen. The path went bounded → architectural, then spec, then Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans after approval.
